tasks.title: A mask for a range of outputs
tasks.statement: Bidirectional DShot is needed on outputs **{a}** through **{b}** inclusive. What value do you write to `SERVO_BLH_BDMASK`?
tasks.solution: The weight of output n is 2^(n − 1). The sum of the weights from a to b: 2^b − 2^(a − 1). The module's example: outputs 1–4 → 16 − 1 = 15; outputs 9–10 → 1024 − 256 = 768.

tasks.title: How many outputs are in the mask
tasks.statement: `BRD_SAFETY_MASK = {v}`. How many outputs keep working with the safety switch engaged?
tasks.solution: Break the number into powers of two: every set bit is one output, and bit 0 is output 1. The module's examples: 4288 = 4096 + 128 + 64 is three outputs (13, 8, 7); 16383 = 2^14 − 1 is fourteen outputs; 16368 = 16383 − 15 is ten outputs (5–14), which is the Copter default for a quadcopter with motors on outputs 1–4.

tasks.title: A surface servo pulse (the "angle" type)
tasks.statement: An output with an "angle" function: `SERVOn_MIN = {mn}`, `SERVOn_MAX = {mx}`, `SERVOn_TRIM = {tr}`, `SERVOn_REVERSED = {r}`. The controller outputs **{p}%** of full travel (full travel is 4500). Find the pulse width in microseconds the way the firmware calculates it.
tasks.solution: s = p · 45; `REVERSED = 1` flips the sign of s. For s > 0: TRIM + ⌊s · (MAX − TRIM) / 4500⌋, otherwise TRIM − ⌊|s| · (TRIM − MIN) / 4500⌋. The fractional part is truncated, not rounded. The module's example: MIN 1000, MAX 1900, TRIM 1520, s = 1500 → 1520 + ⌊126.67⌋ = 1646.

tasks.title: A flap servo pulse (the "range" type)
tasks.statement: An output with a "range" function (H = 100): `SERVOn_MIN = {mn}`, `SERVOn_MAX = {mx}`, `SERVOn_REVERSED = {r}`. The input value is **{u}**. Find the pulse width in microseconds the way the firmware calculates it.
tasks.answer: mn + ((u if r == 0 else 100 - u)*(mx - mn))//100
tasks.solution: PWM = MIN + ⌊s · (MAX − MIN) / 100⌋; with `REVERSED = 1`, s is first replaced with 100 − s. The module's example: MIN 1100, MAX 1950, s = 33 → 1100 + ⌊280.5⌋ = 1380; with the reversal s = 67 → 1100 + ⌊569.5⌋ = 1669.

tasks.title: Motor RPM from ESC telemetry
tasks.statement: An ESC reports an electrical frequency of **{e}** in units of 100 eRPM. `SERVO_BLH_POLES = {n}`. What RPM does the firmware write to the `RPM` field?
tasks.solution: RPM = ⌊E · 200 / poles⌋: a hundred eRPM per unit, two poles per pair. The module's example: E = 1470, 14 poles → 21000 RPM, that is, 350 Hz for the notch filter.

tasks.title: How many outputs are left for servos
tasks.statement: MatekH743, standard build: TIM8 has outputs 1–2, TIM5 has 3–6, TIM4 has 7–10, TIM15 has 11–12. DShot motors are on outputs 1 through **{n}**. How many of outputs 1–12 can be given to servos with 50 Hz PWM?
tasks.solution: A group with at least one DShot output is entirely digital. Count the outputs only in the groups the motors do not touch: motors 1–2 → TIM5, TIM4, TIM15 are free (10 outputs); motors 1–4 → TIM4 and TIM15 (6); motors 1–8 → only TIM15 (2).

tasks.title: DShot frame rate
tasks.statement: The main loop rate is **{l} Hz**, `SERVO_DSHOT_RATE = {p}`, and all motors are on DShot. At what rate (Hz) does the flight controller send DShot frames?
tasks.solution: 0 is a fixed 1000 Hz. Otherwise the rate equals the multiple × the loop rate, but the multiple is raised while the result is below 800 Hz. With a 400 Hz loop: 1 → 800, 2 → 800, 3 → 1200, 4 → 1600.
